To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new actin-like protein, MamK-like is present in Magnetospirillium magneticum AMB1 and that this protein is involved in the formation of magnetosomes.
We have discovered a new actin-like protein in Magnetospirillium magneticum AMB1.

(1) A second mamK-like gene is present in M. magneticum AMB1 genome; (2) MamK-like protein is an actin-like protein that forms filaments in vitro and in vivo; and (3) MamK-like is expressed in wild type and mamK mutant cells and its expression is not affected by deletion of the mamK gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and characterization of a second prokaryotic MamK protein in M. magneticum AMB1.
the identification and characterization of a new mamK-like gene and its product in M. magneticum AMB1, which may have an important role in magnetosome formation.
the identification of new genes involved in magnetosome biomineralization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are at least two actin-like Mam proteins, encoded in two different genomic regions, involved in the assembly and/or alignment of magnetosome chains in M. magneticum.
the magnetosome formation process is encoded in the genomic island and that MamK-like is involved in magnetosome alignment in AMB- 1.
the actin-MamK family of proteins has at least 2 members in M. magneticum AMB1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new mamK-like gene in the genome of AMB-1 and that it encodes an actin-like filament-forming protein.
there are two actin-like Mam genes in the genome and both genes are expressed.
we have identified a new member of a family of prokaryotic proteins that are involved in magnetosome biogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetotaxis machinery is more complex than previously thought.
the magnetosome island is not the only genomic locus encoding genes involved in magnetosome biogenesis and that the magnetosome system is more complex than previously thought.
the magnetosome formation is a complex process involving several genes and gene products that are not all encoded in the same genomic island.
